title: Canonical inventory ledger quantity, phase-1 operator, correction gate, and tested rollback

acceptanceCriteria.description: Inventory quantity is owned by immutable signed movements and the backend read model; routes and React render backend inventoryQuantity and stockStatus without owning balance truth.
Additive preparation and destructive cutover remain separate, repeatable, and fail closed when identity, immutability, nonzero movement, or exact legacy-to-ledger parity is absent.
Tested phase-1 and post-cutover rollback paths restore the appropriate prior-runtime compatibility, tolerate replay, preserve ledger immutability, and refuse use in the wrong rollout phase.
The correction packet is regenerated from the canonical read-only plan at the exact implementation SHA, SHA-verifies its CSV, and exposes no apply mode.

PS-462 is reserved in the repository ledger and the existing inventory Trello card title is synchronized to PS-462; historical ps-439-inventory aliases remain compatibility breadcrumbs and advisory-lock PS-439 is unchanged.

Strict typecheck, production frontend build, all 49 source-of-truth gates, inventory kill switch, shipped/cancelled locks, Print Queue recovery, and sync checkpoint regressions pass without live side effects.

Production movement and cutover are not authorized: the current read-only plan still has 49 mismatches requiring 49 append-only movements totaling +1,000, and production is missing the additive 0073 identity and immutability surface.
The out-of-journal 0073 now has a fail-closed operator and runbook, but production execution plus the later 0074 application mechanism still require separate approval.

sotBypass.details: The signed ledger remains canonical. The emergency cache is rebuilt from that ledger under maintenance and only supports a prior runtime; the rollback never edits ledger history or becomes normal runtime truth.

evidence.proves: PGlite applies both rollout phases, composes concurrent signed movements, deduplicates replay, applies append-only correction, removes the cache, and runs the emergency forward rollback twice.
Invalid phase order, mismatched balances, unidentified legacy writes, and immutable-ledger mutations fail closed; the rollback cannot replace the normal pre-cutover guard.
The forward rollback is idempotent, derives compatibility quantities from the ledger, accepts identified prior-runtime movements, and preserves exact cache-to-ledger parity.

evidence.command: npm run test:ps-462-inventory-preparation-rollout && npm run migrate:ps-462-inventory-preparation
evidence.proves: The operator defaults to a read-only transaction and production preflight observed 1,008 inventory rows, 6,905 ledger rows, ledger quantity -489, zero zero-quantity rows, and all 6,905 rows lacking the new identity surface. Offline integration proves 0073 and its pre-cutover compatibility rollback are repeatable and preserve ledger immutability. No production SQL mutation ran.

evidence.command: npm run inventory:correction-packet:prepare && npm run inventory:reconcile:dry-run
evidence.proves: The ignored PS-462 packet at reviewed SHA cee2f059 has plan d62ccdab, 49 rows, +1,000 units, and CSV SHA f3574469. The aggregate also reports 33,193 missing movements, 189 negative balances, and 1,287 billing-display mismatches. No apply mode or production DML ran.
Two Playwright tests render the backend-owned inventory tuple and verify no real postage or marketplace host is contacted.

evidence.command: npm run test:audit-runtime-schema-readiness through npm run test:sot-guard-pack; inspect drizzle/meta/_journal.json
evidence.proves: Runtime DDL is absent and readiness owns the 0073 frontier. The handwritten 0073/0074 files are not journal entries; 0073 therefore uses the explicit PS-462 operator/runbook while filename-only sequencing remains forbidden.
All 49 mandatory architecture, authorization, durable-worker, lifecycle, billing, inventory, and safety gates pass.
Backend and frontend strict TypeScript checks pass at the reviewed SHA.
The production frontend bundle builds successfully with 2,989 modules transformed.

evidence.command: npm run test:inventory-auto-deduct && npm run test:order-editable-lockdown && npm run test:ps-444-print-queue-recovery && npm run test:ps-409-status-catchup-backlog
evidence.proves: Inventory auto-deduction remains kill-switch protected, shipped/cancelled locks remain active, and Print Queue plus sync reliability regressions stay green.

evidence.proves: The existing inventory card 9LO26Gtc is now titled PS-462 without creating a second card or changing its description, list, labels, or status. Advisory-lock PS-439 remains distinct.

The candidate contains the ledger-only rollout, migration split, test-fixture repair, PS-462 identity, read-only correction generator, fail-closed phase-1 operator/runbook, and both phase-correct rollback paths. No production movement, migration, push, or deployment is included.

verification.command: npm run test:inventory-source-of-truth && npm run test:sot-guard-pack

migrations.rollbackPlan: For phase 1, keep maintenance active and run the compatibility rollback to remove only the insert-identity guard before restoring the prior runtime. After phase 2, use the emergency forward rollback to rebuild stock_qty from the immutable ledger before deploying prior runtime SHA 7d1360fc9ca1500c3df5df095e9ced21145566c2. Correction rollback is append-only inverse movement only.

rollback.strategy: Before cutover, use the phase-1 compatibility rollback only when 0073 committed but the compatible runtime cannot deploy; it removes only the insert guard and preserves immutability. After phase 2, use the forward rollback while writes are stopped to recreate ledger-derived compatibility columns before restoring the prior runtime. Never update, delete, or truncate ledger history.

liveVerification.reason: Only production read-only reconciliation and the new phase-1 operator preflight were run. No correction, migration, Render deployment, commit-parity check, or post-deploy health verification is authorized or complete.
